notes: Eminent domain/condemnation case over Big Bend National Park land and mineral rights under the Relinquishment Act; no bearing on lodging, boarding, or letting of dwellings.

Assault-with-intent-to-rape conviction; 'tourist camp' appears only as the place the injured party stumbled to after the assault for someone to call her a cab. No discussion of lodging arrangements or their legal character.
Aggravated assault conviction arising from a fatal fistfight; appellant merely 'drove around' and ended up at a tourist camp afterward. No lodging-law content.

Illegal liquor possession case turning on search-warrant sufficiency and constructive possession of appellant's private residence; the retrieved 'tourist camp' language is from a citation to a different case (Stewart v. State), not this case's facts.

Theft prosecution; facts describe a tourist camp room and its guest-registration practice, but the court's holding concerns sufficiency of circumstantial evidence of theft, not the legal character of the lodging arrangement itself.

Suit by a tourist-camp operator for unpaid rent and lien foreclosure on household goods, but the entire opinion addresses only appellate procedure (cost bonds, appeal bonds, lost papers); the court never characterizes the underlying occupancy arrangement.
Statutory rape conviction reversed for admission of prejudicial extraneous-offense evidence; the tourist camp is merely the situs of the charged act, with no discussion of lodging law.

Liquor possession case reversed for failure to charge on circumstantial evidence; defendant's employment/residence at a tourist camp is background only, with a separately rented room at her own house being the actual subject of the search — no lodging-law holding.

Suit to set aside a deed for grantor's incapacity; a witness's residence at a tourist camp attached to a beer tavern is offered only as evidence of the grantor's declining mental state, not as lodging-law content.

Zoning-ordinance case sustaining a single-family-district ban on a dentist's home office; concerns professional/business use of a residence under the police power, not the letting of rooms or dwellings to lodgers/boarders for pay.

Motorcycle/truck collision negligence case; mentions of nearby 'boarding and rooming houses for college students' are offered only to characterize traffic conditions on the avenue, with no discussion of lodging law.
Murder conviction reversed for improper impeachment; defendants' tourist-camp cabin is merely where they were staying before the killing. No lodging-law content.

Workers' compensation case turning on whether decedent was a 'Texas employee'; his maintaining headquarters at a tourist camp in Odessa is incidental biographical detail, not a holding on lodging arrangements.

Contract/lien dispute over unpaid wages for constructing tourist-camp apartments, reversed for improperly prejudicial cross-examination on an unrelated union matter; no discussion of lodging law or occupancy characterization.

Premises-liability suit over a railroad's outfit-car housing furnished free to a section foreman as an incident of his employment. The court extensively discusses licensee/invitee/tenant characterization, but there is no compensated letting of a dwelling to a lodger or boarder — the housing was uncompensated, incidental to the employment contract — so it does not bear on the corpus's target doctrine despite the surface-level license/lease vocabulary.
Robbery conviction affirmed; 'Alamo Plaza, a tourist camp' is mentioned only as the pickup point for a taxicab ride post-robbery. No lodging-law content.

Workers' compensation case over a traveling employee's death by carbon monoxide poisoning in a tourist-camp cabin while on business travel; the court's analysis concerns course-of-employment/accident law, not the legal character of the lodging itself.
Burglary conviction reversed for insufficient accomplice-witness corroboration; the accomplice's employment 'at his tourist camp' is passing background, not a subject of the court's analysis.
